queries: LLM task complexity accuracy compute scaling illusion thinking 2025 study

sources_considered.why: Controlled puzzle experiments directly vary complexity and measure accuracy.
Experiments test whether allocating inference computation improves answer performance.
Controlled execution tasks distinguish reliability improvements from broader knowledge or more task attempts.

evidence_items.publisher: Parshin Shojaee and colleagues, NeurIPS 2025; arXiv copy
evidence_items.explanation: Controlled puzzle experiments support the accuracy component: tested models fail beyond sufficient complexity. They do not establish declining economic value across every real-world task.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5, discussion of compute-optimal search and Figure 4
evidence_items.explanation: The experiments show that computation and its allocation can improve final answer performance on a fixed problem distribution. This contradicts the technical reading that additional resources only increase attempted volume, although it does not measure data-center investment returns.

evidence_items.publisher: Akshit Sinha and colleagues, ICLR 2026; arXiv copy

receipt.public_excerpt: more reliable at executing the task

evidence_items.explanation: Controlled experiments find improved reliable execution with larger models even when the task is not knowledge-constrained. This supports a capability gain beyond merely attempting more tasks, with limited generalization from synthetic tasks.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not directly identify the effect of marginal data-center capital expenditure.
Accuracy and execution improvements do not establish positive financial returns.
The economic-value component lacks a specified measure.
